import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Set the style of seaborn
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure with two subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))

# Plot 1: Count of fraud vs non-fraud transactions by transaction type
sns.countplot(data=data, x='transaction_type', hue='is_fraud', ax=axes[0], palette='coolwarm')
axes[0].set_title('Transaction Count by Type and Fraud Status')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Transaction Type')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Count')
axes[0].legend(title='Is Fraud', loc='upper right')

# Plot 2: Average transaction amount by hour of day, split by fraud status
sns.lineplot(data=data, x='hour_of_day', y='amount', hue='is_fraud', ax=axes[1], palette='coolwarm', ci=None)
axes[1].set_title('Average Transaction Amount by Hour and Fraud Status')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Hour of Day')
axes[1].set_ylabel('Average Amount')
axes[1].legend(title='Is Fraud', loc='upper right')

# Save the figure
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Set the style of seaborn
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure with two subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))

# Plot 1: Count of fraud vs non-fraud transactions by transaction type
sns.countplot(data=data, x='transaction_type', hue='is_fraud', ax=axes[0], palette='coolwarm')
axes[0].set_title('Transaction Count by Type and Fraud Status')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Transaction Type')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Count')
axes[0].legend(title='Is Fraud', loc='upper right')

# Plot 2: Average transaction amount by hour of day, split by fraud status
sns.lineplot(data=data, x='hour_of_day', y='amount', hue='is_fraud', ax=axes[1], palette='coolwarm', ci=None)
axes[1].set_title('Average Transaction Amount by Hour and Fraud Status')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Hour of Day')
axes[1].set_ylabel('Average Amount')
axes[1].legend(title='Is Fraud', loc='upper right')
